offending.quoted_text: An adverse credibility determination is not necessarily a death knell to CAT protection.
offending.filing: Petitioners' opening brief, Lnu v. Blanche, No. 24-4790
offending.court_quote: And Sethi twice attributed quotations to real opinions in which the quoted language does not appear: Kamalthas v. INS, 251 F.3d 1279, 1284 (9th Cir. 2001), and Avendano-Hernandez v. Lynch, 800 F.3d 1072, 1080 (9th Cir. 2015).
offending.what_actually_exists: Kamalthas v. INS, 251 F.3d 1279 (9th Cir. 2001) is a real Ninth Circuit opinion; the quoted sentence does not appear in it.

offending.quoted_text: The BIA must consider all evidence of record, including evidence of country conditions, in assessing the possibility of future torture.

offending.what_actually_exists: Avendano-Hernandez v. Lynch, 800 F.3d 1072 (9th Cir. 2015) is a real Ninth Circuit opinion; the quoted sentence does not appear in it.

offending.quoted_text: failure to remember non-material details [about his mistreatment] cannot form the basis of an adverse credibility finding
offending.filing: Petitioners' reply brief, Lnu v. Blanche, No. 24-4790
offending.court_quote: Part of the quote attributed to Bandari v. INS, 227 F.3d 1160, 1167 (9th Cir. 2000), does not appear in that opinion.
offending.what_actually_exists: Bandari is real. It states, at 227 F.3d at 1166: “[a] minor inconsistency in identifying the location of a person's persecution, in light of otherwise consistent testimony, cannot form the basis of an adverse credibility finding.” The brief substituted a different proposition and cited a page one further on.

offending.filing: Petitioners' reply brief, Lnu v. Blanche, No. 24-4790
offending.court_quote: Sethi cited Singh v. Gonzales, 491 F.3d 1090, 1096–97 (9th Cir. 2007), for a proposition related to adverse credibility, but the case does not discuss adverse credibility.
offending.what_actually_exists: Singh v. Gonzales, 491 F.3d 1090 (9th Cir. 2007) is a real opinion but does not discuss adverse credibility.

offending.filing: Petitioners' reply brief, Lnu v. Blanche, No. 24-4790
offending.court_quote: Sethi represented the holding of Zahedi v. INS, 222 F.3d 1157, 1165 (9th Cir. 2000), as concerning affidavits, but the opinion does not discuss affidavits.
offending.what_actually_exists: Zahedi v. INS, 222 F.3d 1157 (9th Cir. 2000) is a real opinion but does not discuss affidavits.

offending.filing: Motion to Correct the Record Re: Errata to Petitioner's Opening Brief, No. 24-4790
offending.court_quote: The replacement citations do not support their intended propositions. Sethi twice cited “Eduardo” for the proposition that “country conditions reports” can corroborate an applicant's fear of persecution. Udo, however, does not discuss country conditions reports or the issue of particularity in such reports.
offending.what_actually_exists: Udo v. Garland, 32 F.4th 1198 (9th Cir. 2022) is real; it mentions country conditions reports once, only to say the reports in a prior case had “little probative value” (id. at 1205).

offending.quoted_text: [t]he Ninth Circuit has held that corroboration from witnesses who cannot appear in person should not be discounted solely due to their absence.
offending.filing: Motion to Correct the Record Re: Errata to Petitioner's Opening Brief, No. 24-4790
offending.court_quote: As modified by the Motion to Correct, Sethi apparently intended to cite Lai, 764 F.3d at 1108, not “Lay,” for the proposition that “[t]he Ninth Circuit has held that corroboration from witnesses who cannot appear in person should not be discounted solely due to their absence.” But Lai does not discuss the weight of testimony from absent witnesses.
offending.what_actually_exists: Lai v. Holder, 764 F.3d 1098 (9th Cir. 2014) is real but does not discuss the weight of testimony from absent witnesses.

controls.cited_for: that the Ninth Circuit has stricken a brief in its entirety where it was composed almost entirely of fabricated or inaccurate citations
controls.court_quote: We have previously stricken a brief in its entirety where the brief was composed almost entirely of fabricated or inaccurate citations. Grant v. City of Long Beach, 96 F.4th 1255, 1257 (9th Cir. 2024).

controls.cited_for: the court's authority to impose discipline authorized by rule and statute
controls.court_quote: We have the authority to impose discipline authorized by rule and statute. See Chambers v. NASCO, Inc., 501 U.S. 32, 40 (1991).

controls.cited_for: that an attorney must check every case citation before filing and cannot delegate that role to AI
controls.court_quote: See, e.g., Noland, 336 Cal. App. 5th at 446 (“Before filing any court document, an attorney must carefully check every case citation, fact, and argument to make sure that they are correct and proper. Attorneys cannot delegate that role to AI, computers, robots, or any other form of technology.” (citation modified)).
